headline: A classroom in VR, with a playable piano
intro: Maxwell Zuber and I recreated a university lab in Unreal Engine. We added classroom props and a piano that responds to a motion controller.
context: University of Michigan · Extended-reality course project · Oct 2022
role: Maxwell Zuber and I built the classroom and its interactions together.

hero.alt: A short first-person tour of the archived Unreal classroom prototype shows its windows, computer benches, props, and motion-controller pointer.
hero.caption: Eight seconds from the archived Unreal prototype recording, cropped to the scene and presented without audio.

metrics.label: student collaborators
metrics.note: We built the project together in Unreal Engine.

metrics.label: piano tones
metrics.note: C, D, E, and G appear in the archived audio assets.

metrics.label: controller interaction
metrics.note: Contact plays a note; buttons change the selection.

question.title: Rebuilding the room
question.text: We recreated the lab's windows, computer stations, fixtures, and layout, then added objects such as a printer, violin, trash can, and discarded math book. The piano gave visitors something to play while exploring the room.

steps.title: Touch a piano key
steps.text: Contact with the motion controller plays a default note.

steps.title: Change the note
steps.text: Controller buttons change the selected note. The archived audio assets include C, D, E, and G.

steps.title: Play a melody
steps.text: The original write-up describes using those four notes to play Mary Had a Little Lamb.

gallery.alt: An illustrated controller points at a four-tone piano diagram beside contact, button selection, and sound-feedback steps.
gallery.caption: A diagram made for this portfolio from the original write-up. It shows the controls; the piano's shape differs from the original model.

finding.title: Trying it in a browser
finding.text: The browser version rebuilds the room with new geometry and generated tones. It keeps the four-note piano interaction and a short tour of the props. The video shows the original Unreal prototype.

details: The original Unreal build survives in the project archive. The playable browser version is a later reconstruction.
The recovered write-up credits the piano to the team without assigning individual components to either of us.
credits: Classroom project by Le Qin and Maxwell Zuber. The archive contains the scene assets and interaction code.
The short clip uses the original prototype footage without audio. The browser version generates its own tones and doesn't reuse the film audio credited in the original build.
